title: Step
description: One agent turn: what the model said, the tool it called, and what came back. Written by the harness, one JSON object per line in steps.jsonl. Attack-specific fields (assistant_text, tool_input values, output_full, output_sent_to_model) may hold <FILL: ...> placeholders in skeleton runs (D-024); every other field is structural and always real.

assistant_text.description: The model's text in this turn; empty string if it only called a tool.

tool_name.description: null when the model replied with text only, and for a malformed turn (tool_call_error present, D-063): such a turn runs nothing and is never a submission.

tool_input.description: The tool call's arguments, as the model sent them. null for a text-only or malformed turn.

tool_call_error.description: Present only on a malformed turn (D-063); absent means the turn was well formed. The harness ran nothing and answered with the fixed error text for this cause.

raw_tool_use.description: The tool-call block or blocks exactly as received, any JSON (D-063). Required with tool_call_error and forbidden without it, so a malformed call stays inspectable while the strict tool_input rules below keep guarding every well-formed one.

raw_stop_reason.description: The stop reason as the model server returned it, when it differs in vocabulary from Converse's (D-060: a local runtime says stop, length, tool_calls).

raw_completion.description: The model's text exactly as a local runtime returned it, before any tool-call parsing (D-060).

output_full.description: Tool output as stored (capped at 1 MiB). null if no tool ran.

output_sent_to_model.description: Exactly what the model was shown (capped, ANSI-stripped). The causal 'first appearance' rule reads this field, never output_full.

stop_reason.description: Bedrock Converse stopReason, recorded as returned; a local backend maps its own vocabulary onto this one and keeps the original in raw_stop_reason (D-060). tests/test_schemas.py checks this list against the installed botocore, so a value added by a future SDK fails a test instead of a real run.

bedrock_request_id.description: Optional here because a local run has none (D-060). That every step of a Bedrock run carries one is checked per run in telemetry.check_consistency, since a step cannot see the manifest.

allOf.description: run_command takes exactly a command string.
submit_flag takes exactly a flag string and returns the same fixed reply (never real output).
A text-only turn (no tool_call_error) ran no tool, so it has no input or output.
raw_tool_use exists only on a malformed turn: a well-formed call is already recorded exactly in tool_input.

A malformed turn (D-063) ran nothing: tool_name, tool_input, output_full and exit_code are null, the raw call is kept, and output_sent_to_model is the fixed error text the model was shown (so everything the model saw still appears verbatim in a step).
